diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, if $G$ has a unique fixed-point, then $(\widehat{\mu}_t)_{t\in\N_0}$ converges $\PROB$-almost surely in $\CW_2$ to the Wasserstein barycenter of $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ with weights $w_1,\ldots,w_K$.

We would like to remark that the operator~$G$ in (\ref{eqn: G-operator}) does not always have a unique fixed-point for general input probability measures $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K\in\CP_{2,\mathrm{ac}}(\R^d)$; see, e.g., Example~3.1 of \citep{alvarez2016fixed} for a concrete counterexample.
However, to the best of our knowledge, sufficient conditions to guarantee the uniqueness of the fixed-point of~$G$ for non-parametric $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K$ is still an open problem.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and introduction claim the algorithm 'is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter' and 'converges to the true W2-barycenter ... in an almost sure sense' without stating the uniqueness-of-fixed-point hypothesis. Theorem 2.1(ii) only guarantees convergence to the barycenter under the additional assumption that G has a unique fixed-point, and Remark 2.5 (following Theorem 2.1) states that G does not always have a unique fixed-point for general non-parametric inputs and that characterizing uniqueness is still open. The unconditional a.s. convergence result (Theorem 2.1(i)) is convergence to a fixed-point of G, which need not be the barycenter when G has multiple fixed-points.

failure_location.quote: This gives rise to a computationally tractable stochastic fixed-point algorithm which is provably convergent to the 2-Wasserstein barycenter.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify every prose convergence claim in the abstract and introduction with the hypothesis that G has a unique fixed-point (or equivalently, restate the headline claim as convergence to a fixed-point of G with convergence to the W2-barycenter as a corollary under uniqueness), so the prose matches Theorem 2.1(ii) and Corollary 3.1(ii).
issues.overall_effect: The abstract and introduction (including contribution (ii)) advertise unconditional a.s. convergence to the W2-barycenter, whereas the formal guarantee is conditional on uniqueness of the fixed-point of G—a condition that the paper itself acknowledges is not guaranteed and whose characterization is open for non-parametric inputs. The formal results (Theorem 2.1, Corollary 3.1) themselves are correctly stated and unaffected.
issues.title: Abstract and introduction overclaim unconditional convergence to the barycenter
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local edit (adding a qualifying clause in two to three sentences in the abstract and introduction). Every formal claim and guarantee in Theorem 2.1, Corollary 3.1, and the supporting results survives unchanged; no new lemma, construction, or replacement argument is needed. The method, convergence result, and empirical scope are all preserved once the uniqueness condition is stated.
